question: Should OpenClaw publish a signed standalone Android APK through GitHub Releases or F-Droid, or keep official Android distribution limited to Google Play plus local archive validation?
rationale: The code can already produce a signed third-party APK locally, but publishing it officially changes signing custody, provenance, sideload security, support expectations, and release operations.

options.title: Approve official signed standalone APK path
options.body: Define the supported flavor, signing/provenance rules, and release asset or F-Droid channel, then implement automation against the existing Android release tooling.

options.title: Keep Google Play as the only official binary channel
options.body: Document that standalone APKs are unsupported and keep android:release:archive as maintainer-local validation only.

options.title: Defer until Android release hardening is complete
options.body: Keep the issue open but block implementation until Android release smoke, signing, and support policy are mature enough for sideloaded assets.

recommendation.title: Approve official signed standalone APK path
recommendation.body: Define the supported flavor, signing/provenance rules, and release asset or F-Droid channel, then implement automation against the existing Android release tooling.
